summary: A light social deduction/negotiation game where animal players jockey for position on a track of enclosures, using hidden victory points as currency to bribe and persuade others into voting them upward. It's fast, chaotic, and lives or dies on the table's willingness to talk, trade favors, and occasionally betray each other for laurels.
praised: Quick, silly, high-energy negotiation with a big player count range
Simple rules that open up lots of table talk and dealmaking
Good as a party-weight filler for groups that enjoy Knizia's negotiation games
criticised: Very swingy and reliant on group dynamics; can feel unsatisfying with quiet or non-negotiating players
Some feel it's a lesser, more randomized reskin of Knizia's earlier negotiation designs (e.g. Medici vs. Strozzi/Intrigue lineage)
Downtime or feel-bad moments when players gang up on a leader

interaction.detail: Players spend hidden victory-point tokens to bribe each other for votes on a shared enclosure track, so almost every turn is a direct negotiation affecting a single communal board state. There is no private tableau of note; the entire game is about converting private points into public influence over others.

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Laurels (the game's only victory currency) are earned mainly by winning bribed majority votes to advance your animal up the enclosure hierarchy, with some extra laurels coming from leftover support tokens at game end.
scoring.how_you_win: Use bribery tokens and shifting alliances to win majority support at each level of the enclosure hierarchy, climbing your animal upward tier by tier; whoever has accumulated the most laurels when the game ends is elected Zoo Mascot.
